description:
Determine whether production-shaped HIP kernels can accelerate Ryser permanent calculations over $\mathbb{F}_3$, $\mathbb{F}_5$, and $\mathbb{F}_7$, and identify the viable kernel and arithmetic design for each field. The study must preserve exact finite-field semantics and may conclude no-go for any field when reproducible evidence does not support GPU acceleration.

## Background

The current HIP paths assign one matrix to a one-thread block and execute the Gray-code Ryser walk sequentially. This leaves most lanes of a 32-lane wavefront inactive, and committed measurements show the $\mathbb{F}_5$ and $\mathbb{F}_7$ paths losing to the best in-tree CPU implementations at measured sizes. The $\mathbb{F}_3$ bipedal representation still offers cheap Boolean arithmetic, but that advantage is distinct from computing the permanent over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and does not by itself establish an efficient GPU execution mapping.

The feasibility study should prototype intra-matrix parallelism, such as independent Gray-code ranges with wave-cooperative row updates and reductions, rather than relying only on batching independent matrices. It must evaluate arithmetic representations independently per field: bipedal Boolean arithmetic for $\mathbb{F}_3$; packed bit planes versus scalar or native modular arithmetic for $\mathbb{F}_5$; and compact native tables or modular arithmetic versus bit-sliced representations for $\mathbb{F}_7$.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A linked study artifact and executable prototype specify and exercise at least one intra-matrix parallel Ryser decomposition that assigns multiple GPU lanes to each matrix, including Gray-range initialization, row-sum updates, row-product reduction, and partial-sum reduction.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every measured candidate returns results exactly equal to an in-tree CPU oracle over $\mathbb{F}_3$, $\mathbb{F}_5$, and $\mathbb{F}_7$ on a deterministic seeded suite covering representative small and medium orders, empty and singleton cases where supported, Gray-range boundaries, and both addition and subtraction transitions; any rejected candidate retains its falsifying correctness evidence.
- [hard] REQ-03: Committed raw receipts compare the current GPU path, every retained prototype, and the best applicable in-tree CPU path under one preregistered protocol for all three fields. The receipts record matrix order, batch size, seed, kernel-only and end-to-end throughput, launch duration, git revision, CPU and GPU models, ROCm and compiler versions, and censoring or failure observations.
- [hard] REQ-04: The study quantifies wave utilization, occupancy-limiting resources, private and shared memory use, transfer and launch overhead, sustained-kernel duration, and watchdog-safe work bounds. It states the supported GPU architecture scope and records compile evidence for every architecture claimed to be supported.
- [hard] REQ-05: The field-by-field comparison explains why the $\mathbb{F}_3$ Boolean representation is valid without treating an odd-characteristic permanent as an $\mathbb{F}_2$ permanent, and measures at least two plausible arithmetic representations for each of $\mathbb{F}_5$ and $\mathbb{F}_7$ before selecting or rejecting a design.
- [hard] REQ-06: A go/no-go decision for each field is supported by the receipts and includes measured crossover conditions or an explicit absence of crossover. Every go decision provides a breakdown-ready production design covering input layout, persistent buffers and streams, bounded-duration launches, per-device initialization, error propagation, tested CPU fallback, and behavioral-equivalence coverage.
- [aspirational] REQ-07: A production-shaped prototype exceeds the best applicable CPU throughput by at least $1.5\times$ at one declared scientifically relevant operating point for each of $\mathbb{F}_5$ and $\mathbb{F}_7$ while remaining within the documented safe launch-duration bound.

## Notes

Use the committed feasibility receipts under `dev/studies/b488f02c/` as baseline evidence, including negative and censored observations. Prototype artifacts and final findings belong in this issue resolved study directory and must remain reproducible from committed commands. Production integration is follow-up work after a go decision.

The $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic background follows [Scheinerman2024]; the study must distinguish Boolean bit-slicing from a field embedding into $\mathbb{F}_2$.
title: Evaluate wave-parallel GPU kernels for finite-field permanents
